definition_zh: 棕色；褐色；棕色的；变成褐色；煎至焦黄；晒黑的；全麦的
definition_en: the colour of coffee or earth, having this colour, to become this colour or to cook food until it turns this colour, and by extension sun-darkened skin or unrefined flour
core_image: 秋天一片晒干的落叶，颜色从浅黄转成深褐
scene: 秋天的树林里，一片叶子从浅黄慢慢变成了深褐色。In the autumn wood a leaf slowly turned brown.
sceneCN: 这里 brown 是「棕色；褐色」（第 1 个义项：像咖啡或泥土那样的颜色）；句意为秋日树林里，一片叶子慢慢变成了深褐色。

pos.zh: 形容词：棕色的；褐色的；晒黑的；全麦的
动词：使变成褐色；煎至焦黄

senses.title: The colour of earth
senses.definition: the colour of coffee, chocolate or soil, a mixture of red, yellow and black
senses.definitionCN: 咖啡、巧克力或泥土那样的颜色，介于红、黄与黑之间
senses.example: She painted the wall a warm brown.
senses.exampleCN: 她把墙刷成了温暖的棕色。
senses.why: Old English brun first meant dark or dusky, and only later settled on the particular colour of earth and wood.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 brun 最初意为昏暗、深色，后来才固定指泥土与木头那种特定的颜色。

senses.title: To turn brown in heat
senses.definition: to become brown, or to cook food until its surface turns brown
senses.definitionCN: 变成褐色，或把食物加热到表面呈褐色
senses.example: Brown the onions before you add the meat.
senses.exampleCN: 先洋葱煎至焦黄，再放肉。
senses.why: Heat darkens food the way autumn darkens a leaf, so the colour word became a cooking verb.
senses.whyCN: 加热使食物变深，就像秋天让叶子变深一样，于是这个颜色词成了烹饪动词。

senses.title: Skin darkened by the sun
senses.definition: having skin made darker by the sun, used in everyday speech
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指皮肤被太阳晒深的
senses.example: He came back from the beach brown and happy.
senses.exampleCN: 他从海边回来，晒得黑黑的，很开心。
senses.why: Sun-darkened skin takes the same colour as earth, so the everyday word for that look is simply brown.
senses.whyCN: 晒深的皮肤和泥土是同一个色调，所以日常就用 brown 来形容这种样子。

senses.title: Wholemeal and unrefined
senses.definition: made with whole grain and not refined, said of bread, rice or flour
senses.definitionCN: 用完整谷粒制成、未经精加工的，用于面包、米或面粉
senses.example: He eats brown rice instead of white rice.
senses.exampleCN: 他吃糙米而不吃白米。
senses.why: Unrefined grain keeps its outer layer and looks brown, so the colour names the less processed food.
senses.whyCN: 未精加工的谷物保留了外层，颜色偏褐，于是这个颜色词用来指加工较少的那种食物。

items.en: Brun meant dark, dusky or shining dark, and it could describe more than one shade.
items.cn: brun 意为深色、昏暗，可以形容不止一种色调。

items.en: German braun and Dutch bruin still mean brown today.
items.cn: 德语 braun 与荷兰语 bruin 至今仍表示棕色。

items.en: The word narrowed to the colour of earth, wood and coffee.
items.cn: 这个词缩小为泥土、木头与咖啡的颜色。

items.en: Today brown also cooks food, describes tanned skin and names wholemeal flour.
items.cn: 今天 brown 还能表示煎至焦黄、晒黑的皮肤以及全麦面粉。

definition_zh: 刷子；画笔；刷、梳；轻擦而过；灌木丛
definition_en: a tool with stiff hairs used for cleaning, painting or tidying, to use such a tool, to touch something lightly while passing, or a mass of low bushes
core_image: 一排密密的硬毛扎在木柄上
scene: 画室里，她把笔尖在颜料盘上轻轻一转，然后落在纸上。She dipped the brush in paint and began to draw.
sceneCN: 这里 brush 是「刷子；画笔」（第 1 个义项：带硬毛或软毛的工具）；句意为她把画笔蘸上颜料，开始作画。

derivatives.zh: 由 brush 加 -y 构成，义为「毛多的；灌木丛生的」
由 brush 加 -ing 构成，义为「刷；梳」

senses.title: The tool with stiff hairs
senses.definition: a tool made of stiff hairs or bristles fixed to a handle, used for cleaning, painting or tidying
senses.definitionCN: 把硬毛或鬃毛固定在柄上做成的工具，用来清洁、绘画或整理
senses.example: She dipped the brush in paint and began to draw.
senses.exampleCN: 她把画笔蘸上颜料，开始作画。
senses.why: Old French brosse named a bundle of twigs used for scrubbing, and that bundle of hairs is still the core of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 brosse 指用来擦洗的一束细枝，那束毛状物至今仍是这个词的核心。

senses.title: To clean or tidy with a brush
senses.definition: to clean, smooth or tidy something with a brush
senses.definitionCN: 用刷子清洁、抹平或整理某物
senses.example: He brushes his teeth twice a day.
senses.exampleCN: 他每天刷两次牙。
senses.why: The noun became a verb, naming the repeated stroke that the tool makes.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成动词，用来指这件工具所做的一来一回的动作。

senses.title: To touch lightly in passing
senses.definition: to touch someone or something lightly while moving past
senses.definitionCN: 经过时轻轻碰到某人或某物
senses.example: Her sleeve brushed against my arm.
senses.exampleCN: 她的袖子擦过我的手臂。
senses.why: A brush stroke is light, so the verb came to mean any light touch that barely makes contact.
senses.whyCN: 刷一下本来就很轻，于是这个动词也指几乎没怎么碰到的轻轻一触。

senses.title: Low bushes and twigs
senses.definition: a mass of small bushes and broken twigs, used without a plural
senses.definitionCN: 一片低矮的灌木与断枝，不用复数形式
senses.example: The rabbit disappeared into the brush.
senses.exampleCN: 兔子钻进灌木丛不见了。
senses.why: The same word names the cut twigs that once made brushes, and later the low growth they came from.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词既指从前扎刷子的断枝，也指后来生长这些枝条的矮丛。

definition_zh: 建造；修建；建立、培养；体格、身材；（逐步）增强
definition_en: to make something by putting parts together, to develop a relationship or quality over time, or the shape and size of a person's body
core_image: 一块砖叠一块砖，慢慢垒成一堵墙
scene: 工地上，工人们一块砖叠一块砖，慢慢砌起一栋房子。Workers laid brick on brick and slowly began to build a house.
sceneCN: 这里 build 是「建造；修建」（第 1 个义项：把材料组合起来盖成东西）；句意为工人们一块砖叠一块砖，慢慢盖起一栋房子。

derivatives.zh: 由 build 加 -er 构成，义为「建造者；建筑工人」
由 build 加 -ing 构成，义为「建筑物；建造」
由 build 加前缀 re- 构成，义为「重建」

senses.title: To put parts together
senses.definition: to make something such as a house or a road by putting materials and parts together
senses.definitionCN: 把材料与部件组合起来，造出房屋、道路等
senses.example: Workers laid brick on brick and began to build a house.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们一块砖叠一块砖，开始盖一栋房子。
senses.why: Old English byldan came from bold, a word for a house, so to build was literally to make a dwelling.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 byldan 来自 bold，也就是「房屋」，所以 build 原义就是造一处住所。

senses.title: To develop over time
senses.definition: to develop something such as trust, a team or a business gradually
senses.definitionCN: 逐步发展出信任、队伍或事业之类的东西
senses.example: It takes years to build trust between neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 邻里之间的信任要花很多年才能建立。
senses.why: A house rises one brick at a time, and trust or a team rises the same slow way.
senses.whyCN: 房子是一块砖一块砖垒起来的，信任与团队也以同样缓慢的方式积累起来。

senses.title: The shape of a body
senses.definition: the shape and size of a person's body, used as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 作名词时指一个人身体的形状与大小
senses.example: The swimmer has a strong build.
senses.exampleCN: 这位游泳运动员体格健壮。
senses.why: How a body is put together is pictured like a structure, so the noun for the body's frame came from the same word.
senses.whyCN: 身体如何被「搭建」起来就像一座结构，所以指身体骨架的名词也出自同一个词。

senses.title: To grow in strength
senses.definition: to increase gradually in amount or strength, especially in the phrase build up
senses.definitionCN: 数量或强度逐渐增加，尤用于 build up 这一短语
senses.example: Traffic builds up quickly after five.
senses.exampleCN: 五点以后车流很快就堵起来了。
senses.why: Layer added to layer makes a wall taller, and anything that grows by layers is said to build up.
senses.whyCN: 一层叠上一层，墙就越来越高；任何一层层增长的东西都可以说 build up。

intro.en: Build began as the verb of an old word for a house, and it has spread from walls to bodies and to trust.
intro.cn: build 最初是一个表示「房屋」的古词的动词形式，后来从墙扩展到体格与信任。

items.en: Bold meant a house or a dwelling, the thing a builder made.
items.cn: bold 意为房屋或住所，也就是建造者所造之物。

items.en: Byldan was the verb built on bold, meaning to make a dwelling.
items.cn: byldan 是建立在 bold 之上的动词，意为造住所。

items.en: Old Norse byggja, to dwell or to build, helped shape the word in the north.
items.cn: 古诺尔斯语 byggja 意为居住、建造，在北方影响了这个词的形态。

items.en: The verb settled as build with built as its past tense.
items.cn: 这个动词固定为 build，过去式为 built。

items.en: Today people build houses, teams, trust and strength, and a build can mean a body.
items.cn: 今天人们 build 房子、团队、信任与力量，而 a build 也可以指体格。

entries.definition: Brave, or a house in old English.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「大胆的」，古英语中又指房屋，与 build 同源。

entries.definition: The past tense and past participle of this verb.
entries.definitionCN: 本词的过去式与过去分词。

entries.definition: An association of workers in one trade.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「行会」，拼写与 build 相近。

entries.definition: To build something large or complex, often in a formal tone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「建造；构筑」，语气较正式。

entries.definition: To make something that did not exist before.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「创造」，指造出原先没有的东西。

entries.definition: To grow or make something grow over time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「发展；培养」。

normal.en: Old English bold meant a house, and byldan was the verb for making one.
normal.cn: 古英语 bold 意为房屋，byldan 就是造房子的动词。

normal.en: A house rises one brick at a time, and trust or a team rises the same way.
normal.cn: 房子一块砖一块砖垒起，信任与团队也以同样方式积累。

normal.en: The way a body is put together is also called a build.
normal.cn: 身体被「搭建」起来的方式也被称作 build。

normal.en: It often pairs with house, team, up and confidence.
normal.cn: 它常与 house、team、up、confidence 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-u-i-l-d; the past tense is built, not builded.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-u-i-l-d；过去式是 built，不是 builded。

abstract.en: See a low wall grow brick by brick until it becomes a house: that growing is to build.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵矮墙一块砖一块砖长高，最后变成房子：这个生长的过程就是 build。

abstract.en: Replace the bricks with promises kept and the same wall becomes trust.
abstract.cn: 把砖换成一次次守住的承诺，同一堵墙就变成了信任。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud, then let the rising wall bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让那堵逐渐升高的墙把意思带回来。

examples.en: Workers laid brick on brick and began to build a house.
examples.cn: 工人们一块砖叠一块砖，开始盖一栋房子。

examples.en: It takes years to build trust between neighbours.
examples.cn: 邻里之间的信任要花很多年才能建立。

examples.en: The swimmer has a strong build.
examples.cn: 这位游泳运动员体格健壮。

root: build 来自古英语 byldan，它建立在 bold（房屋）之上，所以原义就是造一处住所；古诺尔斯语 byggja 又在北方影响了它的形态。这个词从盖房子扩展到建立信任、团队与事业，也从房子扩展到人的体格；由于一层层叠加能让东西变高，它还引申出「逐步增强」的意思。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of build grow from one picture: one brick laid on another until something stands.
sensesIntro.cn: build 的四个义项都从同一个画面生长出来：一块砖叠在另一块砖上，直到某样东西立起来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: brick laid on brick until a wall stands
core.cn: 核心意象：一块砖叠一块砖，直到墙立起来

branches.en: THE HOUSE: putting parts together is the first and literal sense.
branches.cn: 房屋线：把部件组合起来是最字面的第一个义项。

branches.en: THE TRUST: slow layers of action also build a relationship.
branches.cn: 信任线：缓慢积累的行动也能建立关系。

branches.en: THE FRAME: a body put together is its build.
branches.cn: 骨架线：身体被组合起来的样子就是体格。

branches.en: THE PILE: layers added up make traffic or pressure build.
branches.cn: 堆积线：一层层叠加会让车流或压力积聚。

branches.en: THE PATIENCE: a house and trust both rise slowly.
branches.cn: 耐性线：房子与信任都只能慢慢长起来。

definition_zh: 燃烧；烧毁；烧伤、烫伤；发烫、灼热
definition_en: to be on fire, to destroy or damage something with fire or heat, to injure the skin with heat, or to feel very hot
core_image: 橙色火苗舔着一块木头，木头发红发黑
scene: 炉火太旺，锅底的一层油忽然烧了起来。The oil in the pan began to burn.
sceneCN: 这里 burn 是「燃烧」（第 1 个义项：着火、烧起来）；句意为炉火太旺，锅底的那层油忽然烧了起来。

pos.zh: 动词：燃烧；烧毁；灼伤；发烫

derivatives.zh: 由 burn 加 -er 构成，义为「燃烧器；炉头」
由 burn 加 -ing 构成，义为「燃烧的；火热的」
由 sun 与 burn 组合而成，义为「晒伤」

senses.title: To be on fire
senses.definition: to be on fire, or to produce flames and heat
senses.definitionCN: 着火，或产生火焰与热量
senses.example: The oil in the pan began to burn.
senses.exampleCN: 锅底的那层油开始烧了起来。
senses.why: Old English had two verbs, beornan for something already on fire and bærnan for setting it alight.
senses.whyCN: 古英语有两个动词：beornan 指某物自己在烧，bærnan 指点火把它烧起来。

senses.title: To destroy with fire
senses.definition: to destroy or damage something by fire or great heat
senses.definitionCN: 用火或高温毁坏、损坏某物
senses.example: The fire burned down the old barn.
senses.exampleCN: 大火把旧谷仓烧毁了。
senses.why: When fire takes a whole object, the burning ends in nothing, so the verb came to mean destroying as well.
senses.whyCN: 当火吞掉整件东西，燃烧的结局就是化为乌有，于是这个动词也指毁掉。

senses.title: To injure the skin with heat
senses.definition: to hurt or damage the skin with fire, heat or a hot liquid
senses.definitionCN: 用火、高温或热液伤害皮肤
senses.example: She burned her hand on the hot pan.
senses.exampleCN: 她的手被热锅烫伤了。
senses.why: The same heat that feeds a flame also injures flesh, so the verb covers the harm done to a body.
senses.whyCN: 供养火焰的那份热也会伤到皮肉，所以这个动词也指身体受到的伤害。

senses.title: To feel very hot
senses.definition: to feel very hot, or to give out a strong heat, often used of skin or the sun
senses.definitionCN: 感到极热，或散发出强烈的热，常用于皮肤或太阳
senses.example: His forehead was burning with fever.
senses.exampleCN: 他发着烧，额头滚烫。
senses.why: A body on fire and a body with fever feel the same, so the word also describes heat inside a person.
senses.whyCN: 着火的物体和发烧的身体感觉相同，所以这个词也用来形容人体内的热度。

intro.en: Burn comes from two old verbs, one for being on fire and one for setting fire, which merged into a single word.
intro.cn: burn 来自两个古动词，一个指自己着火，一个指点火，二者后来合成一个词。

items.en: Beornan meant to be on fire, used of the thing that burns.
items.cn: beornan 意为正在着火，用于燃烧的那件东西。

items.en: Baernan meant to set something on fire, used of the person who lights it.
items.cn: baernan 意为点燃某物，用于点火的人。

items.en: German brennen and Dutch branden keep both senses in one verb.
items.cn: 德语 brennen 与荷兰语 branden 把一个动词的两种用法都保留下来。

items.en: The two verbs merged into burn, and burnt or burned served as the past form.
items.cn: 两个动词合并为 burn，过去式用 burnt 或 burned。

items.en: Today burn covers fire, destruction, injury and the heat of fever.
items.cn: 今天 burn 覆盖着火、烧毁、灼伤与发烧的热度。

entries.definition: To break open suddenly.

entries.definition: To put something under the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「埋葬；埋藏」，拼写与 burn 相近。

entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「燃起火焰」。

entries.definition: To burn very strongly and brightly.

entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「烤焦表面」。

definition_zh: 公共汽车；巴士；用大巴运送；（计算机）总线
definition_en: a large road vehicle that carries many passengers for a fare, to carry people by such a vehicle, or the channel that carries data inside a computer
core_image: 一辆长长的车厢停在站牌旁，车门打开，乘客排队上车
scene: 清晨的车站，一辆公交车靠站，学生们排队上车。A bus stopped at the corner and the students got on.
sceneCN: 这里 bus 是「公共汽车；巴士」（第 1 个义项：载客收费的大型道路车辆）；句意为一辆公交车在街角停下，学生们上了车。

pos.zh: 名词：公共汽车；巴士；总线

derivatives.zh: 由 bus 与 load 组合而成，义为「一整车的载客量」
由 mini 与 bus 组合而成，义为「小型巴士」
由 bus 与 man 组合而成，义为「公交车司机」

senses.title: A large passenger vehicle
senses.definition: a large road vehicle that carries many passengers along a fixed route for a fare
senses.definitionCN: 沿固定路线载运大量乘客、按票价收费的大型道路车辆
senses.example: A bus stopped at the corner and the students got on.
senses.exampleCN: 一辆公交车在街角停下，学生们上了车。
senses.why: The word is a shortened form of omnibus, Latin for for all, because the vehicle is open to everyone who pays.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 omnibus 的缩略形式，拉丁语意为「给所有人」，因为这辆车对每位付钱的人都开放。

senses.title: To carry people by bus
senses.definition: to carry people somewhere in a bus, especially in groups
senses.definitionCN: 用大巴把人送到某处，尤指成批运送
senses.example: The school buses children from nearby villages.
senses.exampleCN: 学校用大巴把附近村庄的孩子接来。
senses.why: The vehicle turned into a verb, naming the job the vehicle does.
senses.whyCN: 车辆变成了动词，用来指这辆车所做的工作。

senses.title: The data channel in a computer
senses.definition: the shared pathway that carries data between parts of a computer
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机各部件之间传输数据的公共通路
senses.example: A faster bus moves data between the chips quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 更快的总线能在芯片之间快速传输数据。
senses.why: A data path carries many signals along one route, like a bus carrying many passengers.
senses.whyCN: 数据传输通路沿一条线路承载许多信号，就像一辆公交车载着许多乘客。

intro.en: Bus is a clipped form of a French phrase built on the Latin word for all.
intro.cn: bus 是一个法语词组的缩略形式，那个词组建立在拉丁语「全部」一词之上。

items.en: Omnis meant all, and its form omnibus meant for all.
items.cn: omnis 意为全部，其形式 omnibus 意为「给所有人的」。

items.en: A French carriage open to all paying passengers was called voiture omnibus.
items.cn: 一种对每位付费乘客开放的法国马车被称作 voiture omnibus。

items.en: English borrowed omnibus in the 1820s for a large public carriage.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪二十年代借入 omnibus，指大型公共马车。

items.en: Speakers cut the long word to bus, which became the everyday name.
items.cn: 说话人把这个长词截短为 bus，它成了日常名称。

items.en: Today bus is a vehicle, a verb, and even the pathway inside a computer.
items.cn: 今天 bus 既是车辆、动词，甚至也是计算机内部的通路。

root: bus 是法语词组 voiture omnibus 的缩略形式，而 omnibus 来自拉丁语 omnis（全部），意为「给所有人的」，因为这种车对每位付钱的乘客开放。英语在十九世纪二十年代借入 omnibus，后截短为 bus。今天它既是公共汽车，也作动词表示用大巴运送，还指计算机内部传输数据的通路。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses of bus grow from one picture: one long vehicle that carries many people along one route.

definition_zh: 生意；商业；公司、企业；事务；职责
definition_en: the activity of buying and selling goods and services, a company that does this, matters that need attention, or the thing that is properly someone's concern
core_image: 街角小店开门营业，柜台上放着账本与零钱
scene: 街角的小店从早开到晚，生意一直不错。The little shop on the corner does good business all year.
sceneCN: 这里 business 是「生意；商业」（第 1 个义项：买卖商品与服务的活动）；句意为街角那家小店一年到头生意都不错。

pos.zh: 名词：生意；商业；公司；事务；职责

由 business 与 like 组合而成，义为「讲求效率的；公事公办的」

senses.title: Buying and selling
senses.definition: the activity of buying and selling goods or services
senses.definitionCN: 买卖商品或服务的活动
senses.example: The little shop does good business all year.
senses.exampleCN: 那家小店一年到头生意都不错。
senses.why: Business first meant the state of being busy, then the work a person is busy with, and finally trade.
senses.whyCN: business 最初指「忙碌的状态」，接着指一个人忙于做的事，最后指买卖。

senses.title: A company
senses.definition: a company that makes, buys or sells goods or services
senses.definitionCN: 制造、购买或出售商品与服务的公司
senses.example: He runs a small business with his brother.
senses.exampleCN: 他和弟弟一起经营一家小企业。
senses.why: When the buying and selling is set up as an organization, the activity itself becomes the name of the firm.
senses.whyCN: 当买卖被组织成一家机构时，这项活动本身就成了这家公司的名称。

senses.title: Matters to deal with
senses.definition: things that need to be dealt with or discussed
senses.definitionCN: 需要处理或讨论的事情
senses.example: Let us finish the business of the meeting first.
senses.exampleCN: 我们先把会议的事务办完。
senses.why: The old sense of being busy with something survived: any matter that keeps you occupied is your business.
senses.whyCN: 「忙于某事」的旧义保留了下来：任何让你有事可做的事情都叫 business。

senses.title: What properly concerns you
senses.definition: the thing that is properly your concern and not another person's
senses.definitionCN: 本该由你负责、而不是别人的事
senses.example: How I spend my money is my own business.
senses.exampleCN: 我怎么花钱是我自己的事。
senses.why: What a person is busy with is his own concern, so the word also marks the line between my affairs and yours.
senses.whyCN: 一个人忙于的事就是他自己的关切，所以这个词也划出了我的事与你的事之间的界线。

intro.en: Business was formed from busy, and it has moved from the state of being busy to the world of trade.
intro.cn: business 由 busy 构成，词义从「忙碌的状态」一路走到「买卖」。

items.en: Bisignes meant the state of being busy, and also care and anxiety.
items.cn: bisignes 意为忙碌的状态，也指操心与忧虑。

items.en: The noun was built from bisig, busy, with the ending -nes.
items.cn: 这个名词由 bisig（忙碌的）加上词尾 -nes 构成。

items.en: From being busy the word moved to the work one is busy with.
items.cn: 词义从「忙碌」转向一个人忙于其中的工作。

items.en: In the seventeenth century business came to mean trade and commercial dealing.
items.cn: 十七世纪时 business 开始指贸易与商业往来。

items.en: Today business covers trade, firms, matters to handle and personal concerns.
items.cn: 今天 business 覆盖贸易、公司、待办事务与个人分内之事。

entries.definition: Efficient and practical in the way work is done.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「讲求效率的」，由 business 加 like 构成。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「忙碌」，读音与 business 接近但意思不同。

normal.cn: business 就是 busy 加 ness：先指忙碌的状态，再指那件工作。

normal.en: Old English bisignes also meant care and worry, which busy work often brings.
normal.cn: 古英语 bisignes 也指操心与忧虑，而忙碌的工作常常带来这些。

normal.en: By the seventeenth century the busy work had become trade.
normal.cn: 到十七世纪，忙于其中的工作就变成了买卖。

normal.cn: 它常与 do、trip、small、own 搭配。

abstract.en: See a small shop open its shutters at dawn with a ledger on the counter: that shop is doing business.
abstract.cn: 想象一家小店清晨拉起卷帘门，柜台上放着账本：这家店就在做生意。

abstract.en: Change the ledger into a private letter and the same word becomes my own business.
abstract.cn: 把账本换成一封私人信件，同一个词就变成了「我自己的事」。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud, then let the open shutters bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让那扇拉起的卷帘门把意思带回来。

examples.cn: 那家小店一年到头生意都不错。

examples.en: He runs a small business with his brother.
examples.cn: 他和弟弟一起经营一家小企业。

examples.en: How I spend my money is my own business.
examples.cn: 我怎么花钱是我自己的事。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of business grow from one picture: someone busy at a counter with work that is his own.
sensesIntro.cn: business 的四个义项都从同一个画面生长出来：一个人守在柜台后，忙着一件属于他自己的事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small shop busy at its counter from morning to night
core.cn: 核心意象：一家小店从早到晚在柜台后忙碌

branches.en: THE TRADE: buying and selling is the modern centre of the word.
branches.cn: 贸易线：买卖是这个词现代的核心义。

branches.en: THE FIRM: organized trade becomes a company.
branches.cn: 公司线：被组织起来的买卖成为企业。

branches.en: THE MATTER: whatever keeps you busy is a piece of business.
branches.cn: 事务线：任何让你忙碌的事都是一件 business。

branches.en: THE LINE: what is properly yours marks a boundary.
branches.cn: 界线线：该由你负责的事划出一条边界。

branches.en: THE SHOP: activity and organization sit behind one counter.
branches.cn: 店铺线：活动与机构都立在同一个柜台之后。

senses.title: Having a lot to do
senses.definition: having a lot of things to do and little free time
senses.definitionCN: 有许多事要做、几乎没有空闲时间
senses.example: Everyone in the office is busy on Monday morning.
senses.exampleCN: 周一早上，办公室里的每个人都很忙。
senses.why: Old English bisig meant careful, anxious and occupied, and being occupied is still the heart of the word.

senses.title: Full of activity
senses.definition: full of people or activity, or in use, said of a place or a telephone line
senses.definitionCN: 充满人或活动的，或正在使用中，用于地点或电话线
senses.example: The market is always busy on Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 这个市场星期天总是很热闹。
senses.why: A street crowded with people looks the way a person crowded with tasks feels, so the word moved from people to places.
senses.whyCN: 挤满人的街道，就像被任务挤满的人一样，于是这个词从人扩展到了地点。

senses.title: To keep oneself occupied
senses.definition: to keep yourself occupied with something, especially in the phrase busy oneself with
senses.definitionCN: 使自己忙于某事，尤用于 busy oneself with 这一说法
senses.example: She busied herself with the dishes.
senses.exampleCN: 她忙着洗碗。
senses.why: The adjective became a verb: a person gives himself work so that no time stays empty.
senses.whyCN: 形容词变成动词：一个人给自己找活干，好让时间不空着。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud, then let the buried desk bring the meaning back.

sensesIntro.en: All three senses of busy grow from one picture: a person whose hands and time are completely taken up.

branches.en: THE PLACE: a crowd of people makes a street busy.
branches.cn: 地点线：人流聚集使街道变得繁忙。

branches.en: THE ACT: the verb gives oneself work on purpose.
branches.cn: 动作线：动词指有意给自己找活干。

branches.cn: 拥挤线：忙碌的人与繁忙的街道都被塞得满满的。

intro.cn: busy 是基础形容词兼动词，下面列出的是它的词尾以及与之组合的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin occupatus means occupied and negotiosus means full of business; they are parallels, not the source of busy.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 occupatus 意为「被占用的」，negotiosus 意为「事务繁多的」，它们是平行词，不是 busy 的来源。

items.exampleCN: bisig 是有记录的古英语形式。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 the line is busy。

definition_zh: 但是；然而；除了；只、仅仅
definition_en: used to introduce something that contrasts with what was said, to mean except, or in formal use to mean only
core_image: 一条路上横着一块石头，脚要绕过去
scene: 他想出门，但是雨一直没停，只好留在家里。He wanted to go out, but the rain kept him at home.
sceneCN: 这里 but 是「但是；然而」（第 1 个义项：引出与前面相反的情况）；句意为他本想出门，但雨把他留在了家里。

derivatives.zh: 古英语形式，义为「在外；没有」，是 but 的前身
由 but 转作名词后加 -s 构成，义为「异议；推托的借口」

senses.title: Introducing a contrast
senses.definition: used to join two statements that contrast with each other
senses.definitionCN: 用来连接两个彼此形成对照的陈述
senses.example: He wanted to go out, but the rain kept him at home.
senses.exampleCN: 他本想出门，雨却把他留在了家里。
senses.why: The oldest but meant outside or without, so a clause beginning with it stands outside what was just said.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的 but 意为「在外、没有」，所以由它引出的分句站在这之前所说内容的外面。

senses.title: Except
senses.definition: used after words such as all, every or no one to mean except
senses.definitionCN: 用在 all、every、no one 等词之后，表示「除……之外」
senses.example: Everyone but Tom agreed to the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 除了汤姆，大家都同意这个计划。
senses.why: Setting one thing outside the rest is exactly the old sense of being without, which became except.
senses.whyCN: 把一样东西放在其余之外，正是「没有」这个旧义，后来就固定为「除了」。

senses.title: Only
senses.definition: used in a formal or literary way to mean only
senses.definitionCN: 用于正式或文学语境，表示「只、仅仅」
senses.example: We can but try our best.
senses.exampleCN: 我们只能尽力而为。
senses.why: Anything set outside the statement is excluded, and what remains is the single thing allowed, which is only.
senses.whyCN: 被排除在陈述之外的都去掉了，剩下的那唯一一样就是「只」。

intro.en: But began as a word for outside and without, and that idea of exclusion stands behind all its uses.
intro.cn: but 最初表示「在外、没有」，这种排除的意思支撑着它全部的用法。

items.en: Butan meant outside or without, built from be and utan.
items.cn: butan 意为在外、没有，由 be 与 utan 构成。

items.en: Old Norse bta and German ausser carry the same idea of being outside.
items.cn: 古诺尔斯语与德语 ausser 都带有「在外」这层意思。

items.en: With a noun after it, butan came to mean except: all outside this one.
items.cn: 后面跟名词时，butan 逐渐意为「除了」：除这一个之外全都在外。

items.en: The word shortened to but and took on the contrastive sense it has today.
items.cn: 这个词缩短为 but，并发展出今天这种表示转折的用法。

items.en: Today but joins contrasts, marks exceptions and can still mean only in older styles.
items.cn: 今天 but 用来连接转折、标出例外，在较早的文体中仍可表示「只」。

entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「除了……之外」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded history, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的历史、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Old English butan meant outside or without, from be plus utan.
normal.cn: 古英语 butan 意为在外、没有，由 be 与 utan 组成。

normal.en: All but one means everything outside that one, which is exactly except.
normal.cn: all but one 就是除去那一个之外的全部，正好是「除了」。

normal.en: What is left after everything is set outside is only one thing.
normal.cn: 把其余都放到外面之后剩下的那一样，就是「只」。

normal.en: It often pairs with not only, nothing and for.
normal.cn: 它常与 not only、nothing、for 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-u-t; when unstressed it sounds like bət.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-u-t；在句中弱读时读音接近 bət。

abstract.en: See a stone lying across a path, so the foot has to go around it: that turn is but.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石头横在小路上，脚只得绕过去：这个转折就是 but。

abstract.en: Leave one stone out of the whole pile and the same picture becomes except.
abstract.cn: 把一块石头从整堆里拿出来，同一幅画面就变成了「除了」。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud, then let the stone on the path bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让那块横在路上的石头把意思带回来。

examples.en: He wanted to go out, but the rain kept him at home.
examples.cn: 他本想出门，但雨把他留在了家里。

examples.en: Everyone but Tom agreed to the plan.
examples.cn: 除了汤姆，大家都同意这个计划。

examples.en: We can but try our best.
examples.cn: 我们只能尽力而为。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「巴特」——路中间横着石头，脚只能绕过去：但是

root: but 来自古英语 butan，由 be 与 utan 构成，原意为「在外、没有」。后面跟名词时，它逐渐表示「除这一个之外全都在外」，也就是「除了」；到了中古英语，词形缩短为 but，并发展出今天这种表示转折的用法；被排除在外的都去掉之后，剩下的唯一一样便是「只」。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses of but grow from one idea: putting something outside the rest.
sensesIntro.cn: but 的三个义项都从同一个想法生长出来：把某样东西放到其余之外。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone lying across a path that the foot must go around
core.cn: 核心意象：一块横在小路上、脚必须绕过的石头

branches.en: THE TURN: a clause outside the first one turns the sentence.
branches.cn: 转折线：站在前一句之外的分句让句子拐了个弯。

branches.en: THE EXCEPTION: one thing is set outside the rest.
branches.cn: 例外线：把一样东西放到其余之外。

branches.en: THE SINGLE: what remains outside is the only thing left.
branches.cn: 唯一线：被留在外面的那一样就是仅剩的。

branches.en: THE EDGE: contrast and exception both draw an edge.
branches.cn: 边缘线：转折与例外都在划一条边。

branches.en: THE REMAINDER: except and only name two views of the same remainder.
branches.cn: 余量线：except 与 only 是同一份余量的两种看法。

intro.en: But is a small base word with no endings of its own, so the items below are the parts it came from and the phrases it joins.
intro.cn: but 是没有自身词尾的基础小词，下面列出的是它的构成成分以及与之组合的短语。

latinIntro.en: Latin sed means but and praeter means except; they are parallels, not the source of but.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sed 意为「但是」，praeter 意为「除了」，它们是平行词，不是 but 的来源。

items.example: It is the first part of butan.
items.exampleCN: 它是 butan 的第一部分。

items.example: It is the second part of butan.
items.exampleCN: 它是 butan 的第二部分。

items.meaning: the first of two added items
items.meaningCN: 两个并列项中的前一项
items.example: It forms not only but also.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 not only but also。

items.example: It forms last but not least.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 last but not least。

definition_zh: 黄油；涂黄油于；（口语）奉承、讨好
definition_en: a soft yellow food made from cream and spread on bread, to spread it on food, or in informal speech to flatter someone
core_image: 一块淡黄色、表面带刀痕的黄油放在面包旁
scene: 早餐桌上，她把一小块黄油抹在刚烤好的吐司上。She spread butter on the warm toast.
sceneCN: 这里 butter 是「黄油」（第 1 个义项：用奶油制成的黄色软食）；句意为她把黄油抹在温热的吐司上。

collocations.zh: 面包与黄油；主要收入来源

derivatives.zh: 由 butter 加 -y 构成，义为「含黄油的；黄油般的」
由 butter 与 milk 组合而成，义为「酪乳」
由 butter 与 fly 组合而成，义为「蝴蝶」，名字来自旧时对黄色翅膀的联想

senses.title: The yellow food from cream
senses.definition: a soft yellow food made from cream, spread on bread or used in cooking
senses.definitionCN: 用奶油制成的淡黄色软食，涂在面包上或用于烹饪
senses.example: She spread butter on the warm toast.
senses.exampleCN: 她把黄油抹在温热的吐司上。
senses.why: The word travelled from Greek through Latin, where boutyron literally meant cow cheese.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从希腊语经由拉丁语传来，其中 boutyron 字面意思就是「牛的奶酪」。

senses.title: To spread butter on
senses.definition: to put butter on bread or another food
senses.definitionCN: 把黄油涂在面包或其他食物上
senses.example: Butter the pan before you add the eggs.
senses.exampleCN: 打鸡蛋之前先在锅里抹一层黄油。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb, naming the everyday act of spreading it.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成动词，用来指抹黄油这个日常动作。

senses.title: To flatter someone
senses.definition: to flatter someone so that they will help you, used in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指奉承某人，好让对方帮自己
senses.example: He tried to butter up the teacher before the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 考试前他试着讨好老师。
senses.why: Soft butter spreads easily, and smooth flattery spreads over a person the same way.
senses.whyCN: 软黄油很容易抹开，顺耳的奉承也以同样的方式铺到人身上。

intro.en: Butter came into English from Latin, which had taken it from Greek, and the Greek word meant cow cheese.
intro.cn: butter 从拉丁语进入英语，而拉丁语又是从希腊语借来的，希腊语原词意为「牛的奶酪」。

items.en: Boutyron joined bous, cow, with tyros, cheese.
items.cn: boutyron 把 bous（牛）与 tyros（奶酪）组合在一起。

items.en: Latin took the word as butyrum and used it for the yellow fat.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 butyrum，用来指这种黄色的油脂。

items.en: Old English borrowed butere, most likely through church and kitchen Latin.
items.cn: 古英语借入 butere，很可能经由教会与厨房使用的拉丁语。

items.en: German Butter and Dutch boter show the same borrowed word across the north.
items.cn: 德语 Butter 与荷兰语 boter 显示这个词在北方各地同样被借用。

items.en: Today butter is a food, a verb and, in slang, a way of flattering.
items.cn: 今天 butter 是食物、动词，俚语中还指奉承。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects dairy foods.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收乳制品。

entries.definition: An insect with large coloured wings.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蝴蝶」，由 butter 与 fly 构成。

entries.definition: A thick liquid mixture of flour and eggs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「面糊」，拼写与 butter 相近。

entries.definition: Of higher quality than something else.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「更好的」，读音与 butter 接近。

normal.cn: 希腊语 boutyron 字面意为「牛的奶酪」，后来成了 butter。

normal.cn: 拉丁语 butyrum 把这个词带进了欧洲的厨房。

normal.cn: 软黄油容易抹开，所以 buttering someone up 就是顺耳的奉承。

normal.en: It often pairs with bread, peanut, toast and up.
normal.cn: 它常与 bread、peanut、toast、up 搭配。

normal.cn: 拼写是 b-u-t-t-e-r，双写的 t 让元音保持短促。

abstract.en: See a pale yellow block with a knife mark beside warm bread: that block is butter.
abstract.cn: 想象面包旁放着一块带刀痕的淡黄色固体：那块东西就是 butter。

abstract.en: Imagine the same smooth block turned into words and it becomes flattery.
abstract.cn: 想象同一块柔滑的东西变成了话语，它就变成了奉承。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud, then let the yellow block bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让那块黄色的东西把意思带回来。

examples.cn: 她把黄油抹在温热的吐司上。

examples.cn: 打鸡蛋之前先在锅里抹一层黄油。

root: butter 来自古英语 butere，其源头是拉丁语 butyrum，再上溯到希腊语 boutyron，由 bous（牛）与 tyros（奶酪）组合而成，字面意思是「牛的奶酪」。这个词随厨房与教会拉丁语传遍欧洲，德语 Butter 与荷兰语 boter 都是同一借词。今天 butter 既是食物，也作动词表示涂黄油，口语中还指奉承讨好。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses of butter grow from one picture: a soft yellow block that spreads smoothly.
sensesIntro.cn: butter 的三个义项都从同一个画面生长出来：一块容易抹开的淡黄色软物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pale yellow block of butter beside warm bread
core.cn: 核心意象：面包旁放着一块淡黄色的黄油

branches.en: THE FOOD: the yellow fat itself is the first sense.
branches.cn: 食物线：这种黄色油脂本身是第一个义项。

branches.en: THE SPREAD: the verb names the everyday act of spreading it.
branches.cn: 涂抹线：动词指把它抹开这个日常动作。

branches.en: THE FLATTERY: smooth spreading becomes smooth talk.
branches.cn: 奉承线：柔滑的涂抹变成了顺耳的话语。

branches.en: THE TABLE: food and spreading happen at the same breakfast.
branches.cn: 餐桌线：食物与涂抹发生在同一顿早餐里。

branches.en: THE SMOOTHNESS: butter and flattery both go on easily.
branches.cn: 柔滑线：黄油与奉承都很容易铺上去。

intro.en: Butter is a base noun and verb, so the items below are its endings and the words it joins.
intro.cn: butter 是基础名词兼动词，下面列出的是它的词尾以及与之组合的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin butyrum is the recorded form that brought the word to English; it is the direct source, not a mere parallel.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 butyrum 是把这个词带进英语的有记录形式，它是直接来源，不只是平行词。

items.example: Butyrum is the recorded Latin source.
items.exampleCN: butyrum 是有记录的拉丁语来源。

definition_zh: 买；购买；买来的东西、合算的货；（口语）相信、接受
definition_en: to get something by paying money for it, something worth the money paid, or in informal speech to believe an idea
core_image: 手里递出钱，换回一件想要的东西
scene: 菜市场里，她挑了两斤番茄，付钱给摊主。She bought two kilos of tomatoes from the stall.
sceneCN: 这里 buy 是「买；购买」（第 1 个义项：付钱换取东西）；句意为她从摊位上买了两公斤番茄。

pos.zh: 名词：买来的东西；合算的货

derivatives.zh: 由 buy 加 -er 构成，义为「买主；采购员」
由 buy 与 out 组合而成，义为「收购全部股份」
由 buy 加前缀 re- 构成，义为「再次购买」

senses.title: To get something with money
senses.definition: to get something by paying money for it
senses.definitionCN: 付钱以取得某物
senses.example: She bought two kilos of tomatoes from the stall.
senses.exampleCN: 她从摊位上买了两公斤番茄。
senses.why: Old English bycgan meant to pay for or redeem, and paying has stayed at the centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 bycgan 意为付款取得或赎回，付钱这个动作一直是这个词的核心。

senses.title: Something worth the price
senses.definition: a thing bought, especially one that is good value for the money
senses.definitionCN: 买来的东西，尤指价钱合算的
senses.example: This bike was a good buy.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆自行车买得很合算。
senses.why: The act turned into a noun, so the thing obtained by the act could be called a buy.
senses.whyCN: 动作转成了名词，于是由这个动作得到的东西也可以叫 a buy。

senses.title: To believe an idea
senses.definition: to believe or accept an explanation, used in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指相信或接受某种说法
senses.example: I don't buy that excuse.
senses.exampleCN: 我不相信那个借口。
senses.why: Accepting an idea is like paying for it: you take it in only if it seems worth the price.
senses.whyCN: 接受一个说法就像为它付钱：只有觉得值这个价，你才会把它收下。

intro.en: Buy is an old Germanic verb for getting something by payment, and its noun and slang senses came much later.
intro.cn: buy 是一个表示「付钱取得」的古老日耳曼动词，名词与俚语义项出现得晚得多。

items.en: Bycgan meant to buy or to redeem something by payment.
items.cn: bycgan 意为购买，或通过付款赎回某物。

items.en: Gothic bugjan carried the same sense of buying and paying.
items.cn: 哥特语 bugjan 带有同样「购买、付款」的意思。

items.en: The past tense bought and the modern shape buy settled in this period.
items.cn: 过去式 bought 与现代词形 buy 都在这一时期固定下来。

items.en: In the nineteenth century a buy could name a bargain as well as the act.
items.cn: 十九世纪时 a buy 既可以指购买行为，也可以指一件合算的货。

items.en: In the twentieth century to buy an idea came to mean to believe it.
items.cn: 二十世纪时 to buy an idea 开始表示「相信某个想法」。

entries.definition: Having a lot to do.

entries.definition: To give something in return for money.

abstract.cn: 想象一只手把硬币递过柜台，又拿回一个红番茄：这个交换就是 buy。

abstract.en: Put a doubtful excuse instead of the tomato and the same exchange becomes believing.
abstract.cn: 把番茄换成一个可疑的借口，同一个交换就变成了「相信」。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud, then let the coin on the counter bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让柜台上那枚硬币把意思带回来。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses of buy grow from one picture: goods and money changing hands across a counter.
sensesIntro.cn: buy 的三个义项都从同一个画面生长出来：货物与钱在柜台两端互换。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: money handed over and goods received
core.cn: 核心意象：递出钱，换回东西

branches.en: THE ACT: paying for goods is the first and literal sense.
branches.cn: 动作线：付钱换取货物是最字面的第一个义项。

branches.en: THE GOODS: the thing obtained can be called a buy.
branches.cn: 货物线：换回的东西本身可以叫 a buy。

branches.en: THE IDEA: accepting a story works like paying for it.
branches.cn: 想法线：接受一个说法就像为它付钱。

branches.en: THE COUNTER: act and object meet at the same counter.
branches.cn: 柜台线：动作与物件在同一张柜台相遇。

branches.en: THE VALUE: a bargain and a believable story both seem worth it.
branches.cn: 价值线：合算的货与可信的说法都显得值当。

senses.title: Beside or near
senses.definition: near or beside a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 在某个人或某物的近旁
senses.example: She stood by the window and watched the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 她站在窗边看着雨。
senses.why: Old English bi meant near or about, and physical closeness is still the most concrete sense.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 bi 意为「在近旁、在周围」，物理上的靠近至今仍是最具体的义项。

senses.title: By means of
senses.definition: used to show the means or method used to do something
senses.definitionCN: 用来表示做某事所用的手段或方法
senses.example: We came by bus and left by train.
senses.exampleCN: 我们乘公交车来，坐火车离开。
senses.why: The help that stands beside you becomes the way you act, so near turned into by means of.
senses.whyCN: 站在你身边的人或物成了你行动所依靠的方式，于是「在旁」变成了「凭借」。

senses.title: Not later than
senses.definition: not later than a stated time or date
senses.definitionCN: 不晚于某个说明的时间或日期
senses.example: Please hand in the form by Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 请在星期五之前交表。
senses.why: If a thing must be beside a point in time, it can arrive before that point but not after it.
senses.whyCN: 如果一件事必须处在一个时间点的旁边，它可以在该点之前到达，但不能在之后。

senses.title: Naming the doer
senses.definition: used after a passive verb to name the person or thing that does the action
senses.definitionCN: 用在被动动词之后，引出实施动作的人或物
senses.example: The song was written by a young student.
senses.exampleCN: 这首歌是一位年轻学生写的。
senses.why: The doer stands right beside the action as its source, and English marks that closeness with by.
senses.whyCN: 施动者紧挨着动作站立，是动作的来源，英语就用 by 来标记这份贴近。

intro.en: By is an old word for near, and nearness slowly turned into means, deadline and the doer of an action.
intro.cn: by 是一个表示「靠近」的古老词，靠近慢慢引申为手段、期限与动作的实施者。

root: by 来自古英语 bi，意为在某物近旁、周围，与德语 bei、荷兰语 bij 同源。因为站在你旁边的东西往往会帮到你，「靠近」引申为标记手段；若一件事必须在某个时间点旁边，便有了「不迟于」；被动句里施动者也被放在动词旁边，于是 by 又用来引出动作的实施者。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of by grow from one idea: being right beside something, in space, in method, in time or in action.
sensesIntro.cn: by 的四个义项都从同一个想法生长出来：在某物近旁，无论是空间、手段、时间还是动作。

branches.cn: 手段线：站在你旁边的东西就是你所借用的。

branches.en: THE TIME: a task must be beside the hour, not after it.
branches.cn: 时间线：任务必须落在那个时点旁边，而不能在后。

branches.en: THE DOER: the agent is placed beside the passive verb.
branches.cn: 施动线：施动者被放在被动动词旁边。

branches.en: THE TOOL: a thing nearby and a thing used are one closeness.

definition_zh: 再见；再会；（比赛中的）轮空；（旧用法）顺便一提
definition_en: a short word said when leaving, a position in a tournament where a player advances without playing, or in older use something said in passing
core_image: 门口挥手告别的两个人
scene: 校门口，男孩背起书包，朝同学挥了挥手说了声再见。The boy waved at his friend and said bye at the school gate.
sceneCN: 这里 bye 是「再见」（第 1 个义项：离开时说的告别语）；句意为男孩在校门口朝朋友挥手说再见。

derivatives.zh: 由 bye 扩展而成的完整告别语，义为「再见」

senses.title: A word said when leaving
senses.definition: a short informal word said when you leave someone
senses.definitionCN: 离开某人时说的简短随意的话
senses.example: The boy waved at his friend and said bye at the school gate.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩在校门口朝朋友挥手说再见。
senses.why: Bye is a worn-down piece of goodbye, which began as a blessing: God be with you.
senses.whyCN: bye 是 goodbye 磨损后的片段，而 goodbye 原本是一句祝福：「愿上帝与你同在」。

senses.title: A free pass in a tournament
senses.definition: a position in a tournament in which a player moves on without playing a match
senses.definitionCN: 比赛中不用交手即可进入下一轮的位置
senses.example: Our team got a bye in the first round.
senses.exampleCN: 我们队在第一轮轮空。
senses.why: A player left standing beside the draw, with no opponent, is said to have a bye.
senses.whyCN: 在抽签表旁没有对手、直接站着的那位选手，就被说成拿到了 bye。

senses.title: Something said in passing
senses.definition: a side remark, kept mostly in the old phrase by the bye
senses.definitionCN: 附带的一句话，今多保留在旧短语 by the bye 中
senses.example: By the bye, your letter arrived this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 顺便说一句，你的信今天早上到了。
senses.why: A remark standing beside the main point is a by-thing, and the old spelling bye kept that meaning.
senses.whyCN: 站在要点旁边的一句话就是附带的事，旧的拼写 bye 保留了这层意思。

items.en: In fast speech the phrase shrank into goodbye, and later into bye.
items.cn: 在快速说话中，这句话缩成 goodbye，后来又缩成 bye。

items.en: A player with no opponent in a round was said to stand by, and the place was called a bye.
items.cn: 某轮没有对手的选手被说成「站在一旁」，这个位置就叫 bye。

items.cn: 旧短语 by the bye 指在主话题旁边顺带说出的话。

items.en: Today bye is mostly a friendly farewell, with the sporting sense still alive.

definition_zh: 蛋糕；饼状的块；（泥等）结成硬块
definition_en: a sweet food baked from flour, sugar and eggs, a flat block of a soft solid, or to form a hard layer when dry
core_image: 生日桌上插着一根蜡烛的小圆蛋糕
scene: 生日聚会上，她把蜡烛插在蛋糕上。She put the candles on the cake.

senses.title: The baked sweet food
senses.definition: a sweet food made from flour, sugar, eggs and fat, baked in an oven
senses.definitionCN: 用面粉、糖、蛋和油脂混合后烤成的甜点
senses.example: She put the candles on the cake.
senses.exampleCN: 她把蜡烛插在蛋糕上。
senses.why: The Norse word kaka named a flat baked food, and English kept the shape of that idea.
senses.whyCN: 古诺斯语 kaka 指一种扁平的烤制食物，英语沿用了这个形状上的概念。

senses.title: A flat block of something
senses.definition: a flat round block of a soft solid, such as soap or mud
senses.definitionCN: 柔软固体压成的一块扁圆物，如肥皂或泥
senses.example: He bought a cake of soap for the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 他为这次出行买了一块肥皂。
senses.why: The flat round shape of a cake was borrowed for soap, wax and mud pressed into blocks.
senses.whyCN: 蛋糕扁圆的形状被借去形容压成块的肥皂、蜡和泥。

senses.title: To form a hard layer
senses.definition: to cover something with a hard layer as it dries
senses.definitionCN: 泥等干后在某物表面结成硬层
senses.example: Mud caked his boots after the long walk.
senses.exampleCN: 长途步行后，泥在他的靴子上结了硬块。
senses.why: When mud dries it sets like a baked crust, so the food word turned into a verb.
senses.whyCN: 泥干后像烤过的外壳一样变硬，于是这个食物词又变成了动词。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses of cake grow from one picture: a flat round mass that sets firm.

branches.en: THE SWEET FOOD: the baked sweet itself is the first sense.

branches.cn: 块状线：扁圆的形状用来指肥皂和蜡。

branches.en: THE HARD LAYER: dried mud sets like a baked crust.
branches.cn: 硬壳线：干泥像烤过的外壳一样变硬。

branches.en: THE SHAPE: the same round form serves food and soap.
branches.cn: 形状线：同一个圆块形状供食物与肥皂共用。

branches.en: THE SETTING: block and hard layer both come from a mass pressed or dried.

senses.title: The chart of the year
senses.definition: a chart that shows the days, weeks and months of a year
senses.definitionCN: 显示一年中日期、星期与月份的表格
senses.example: Every January she circles family birthdays on the calendar.
senses.exampleCN: 每年一月她都在日历上圈出家人的生日。
senses.why: The Latin kalendae named the first day of each month, and the list of those days became the calendar.

senses.title: The system of arranging days
senses.definition: a system that fixes the length and order of months and years
senses.definitionCN: 规定月份与年份长度和顺序的体系

senses.why: Once the chart of days grew into a rule for counting whole years, it was also called a calendar.

senses.title: A list of planned dates
senses.definition: a list of events and the dates on which they will happen
senses.definitionCN: 列有活动及其日期的清单
senses.example: The school calendar lists every exam week.

senses.why: Modern offices turned the paper chart into a schedule, and the same word followed.

root: calendar 可上溯到拉丁语 kalendae，指罗马每月的初一，那天人们要登记账目。由此产生的 calendarium 就是账本，里面按顺序列出每个月的初一。这个词经古法语 calendier 进入英语，写成 calendar，既指月份表，也指账本。后来它分化为两层意思：纸面的日期表格是「日历」，背后的记日规则是「历法」；现代办公又把同一份表格变成排活动的「日程表」。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses of calendar grow from one picture: an ordered list of days.
sensesIntro.cn: calendar 的三个义项都从同一个画面生长出来：一份按顺序排好的日子清单。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: the rule behind the list is the second sense.
branches.cn: 体系线：清单背后的规则是第二个义项。

branches.en: THE PLAN: the same list used for events is the third sense.
branches.cn: 计划线：同一份清单用来排活动就是第三个义项。

branches.en: THE ORDER: chart and system both depend on counting days.

definition_zh: 打电话；呼喊；称呼；短暂拜访
definition_en: to telephone someone, to say something loudly, to give a name to someone, or to visit someone briefly
core_image: 一只手把手机贴在耳边
scene: 晚饭后，她给外婆打了个电话。After dinner she called her grandmother.
sceneCN: 这里 call 是「打电话」（第 1 个义项：用电话与人联系）；句意为晚饭后她给外婆打了个电话。

pos.zh: 动词：打电话；呼喊；称呼；拜访

derivatives.zh: 由 call 加 -er 构成，义为「打电话的人；来访者」
由 call 加 -ing 构成，义为「使命；天职」

senses.title: To telephone someone
senses.definition: to speak to someone by phone
senses.definitionCN: 用电话与某人说话
senses.example: After dinner she called her grandmother.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭后她给外婆打了个电话。
senses.why: Early telephones needed an operator to call out a name, and that act gave the word its modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 早期电话要由接线员喊出对方的名字，这个动作让这个词有了今天的电话义。

senses.title: To say something loudly
senses.definition: to shout or say something in a loud voice
senses.definitionCN: 大声喊出或说出某事
senses.example: He called my name across the street.
senses.exampleCN: 他在街对面喊我的名字。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply to raise the voice, which is where the word began.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思就是提高嗓门，这正是这个词的起点。

senses.title: To give someone a name
senses.definition: to use a particular name or word for someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 用某个名字或词来指称某人某物
senses.example: Everyone calls him Tom.
senses.exampleCN: 大家都叫他汤姆。
senses.why: Calling out a name turned into the fixed name itself, so the verb came to mean to name.
senses.whyCN: 喊出一个名字逐渐变成固定的称呼，于是动词又有了命名的意思。

senses.title: To visit briefly
senses.definition: to make a short visit to a person or place
senses.definitionCN: 到某人处或某地作短暂停留
senses.example: We called on our neighbours after lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 午饭后我们去看望了邻居。
senses.why: A call was once a short stop on a journey, and the visit sense grew from that.
senses.whyCN: call 原指旅途中的短暂停留，拜访义由此发展而来。

intro.en: Call came from Old Norse kalla, to cry out, and the sound of a raised voice is still at its centre.
intro.cn: call 来自古诺斯语 kalla，意思是大声喊，提高嗓门的动作至今仍是它的核心。

items.en: Kalla meant to cry out or summon someone by voice.

items.cn: 古英语 ceallian 带着同样的喊叫义。

items.en: Middle English callen widened to naming and summoning.

normal.en: Old Norse kalla meant to cry out, so call still starts with a raised voice.

definition_zh: 平静的；镇静的；风平浪静的；使平静
definition_en: quiet and not worried, still and without wind, or to make someone or something quiet
core_image: 无风的海面像镜子一样平
scene: 暴风雨过后，海面重新变得平静。After the storm the sea grew calm again.
sceneCN: 这里 calm 是「风平浪静的」（第 3 个义项：海面或天气无风无浪）；句意为暴风雨过后海面重新平静下来。

senses.title: Not worried or excited
senses.definition: quiet and peaceful, not worried or excited
senses.definitionCN: 安静平和，不焦虑也不激动
senses.example: She stayed calm while the others shouted.
senses.exampleCN: 别人都在喊叫时她保持镇静。
senses.why: The word first described the still air of a windless day, then the same stillness inside a person.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初形容无风之日的静止空气，后来也形容人内心的同样静止。

senses.title: To make someone quiet
senses.definition: to make a person or animal become quiet and relaxed
senses.definitionCN: 使人或动物安静放松下来
senses.example: The nurse calmed the frightened child.
senses.exampleCN: 护士安抚了受惊的孩子。
senses.why: If wind can drop, a person can be made to drop too, so the adjective turned into a verb.
senses.whyCN: 风能停下来，人也能被安抚下来，于是形容词变成了动词。

senses.title: Still, without wind
senses.definition: of the sea or weather, still and without wind
senses.definitionCN: 指海面或天气静止无风
senses.example: After the storm the sea grew calm again.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨过后海面重新平静下来。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: the flat, unbroken surface of water on a windless day.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的意思：无风之日平坦无波的水面。

items.en: Kauma meant the burning heat of noon, the hour when the wind falls.
items.cn: kauma 指正午灼热，那是风停下来的时刻。

items.en: Latin cauma kept the sense of midday heat and stillness.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cauma 保留了正午炎热与静止的意思。

items.en: Italian calma shifted from heat to the stillness of the air and sea.
items.cn: 意大利语 calma 从炎热转向空气与海面的静止。

items.cn: 法语 calme 把天气的平静带进了英语。

items.cn: 英语把 calm 从海面扩展到内心，并把它变成了动词。

normal.en: Greek kauma was the noon heat, the hour when the wind drops and the sea flattens.
normal.cn: 希腊语 kauma 指正午的炎热，那时风停、海面变平。

normal.en: Italian calma moved from heat to stillness, and English borrowed that stillness.
normal.cn: 意大利语 calma 从炎热转向静止，英语借来的正是这份静止。

normal.en: A calm sea and a calm mind share the same flat, unbroken surface.
normal.cn: 平静的海与平静的心共享同一片平坦无波的水面。

normal.en: It often pairs with down, keep, stay and sea.
normal.cn: 它常与 down、keep、stay、sea 搭配。

normal.en: Spell c-a-l-m; the l is silent, so it sounds like karm.
normal.cn: 拼写是 c-a-l-m，其中 l 不发音，读起来像 karm。

abstract.en: See a mirror-flat sea with no wind: that surface is calm.
abstract.cn: 想象一片没有风、像镜子一样平的海面：那片水面就是 calm。

abstract.en: Let a worried face mirror that flat water and it becomes a calm mind.
abstract.cn: 让一张焦虑的脸映出那片平水，它就变成了平静的心。

abstract.en: Hold the flat sea in mind and it will flatten your worry when you say the word.
abstract.cn: 记住那片平海，说这个词时它会把你的焦虑也抚平。

examples.en: She stayed calm while the others shouted.
examples.cn: 别人都在喊叫时她保持镇静。

examples.en: The nurse calmed the frightened child.
examples.cn: 护士安抚了受惊的孩子。

examples.en: After the storm the sea grew calm again.
examples.cn: 暴风雨过后海面重新平静下来。

root: calm 很可能来自希腊语 kauma，指正午的灼热，那是一天中风停下来、海面变平的时刻。这个词经拉丁语 cauma 进入意大利语，写成 calma，意思从炎热转到空气与海面的静止，再由法语 calme 传入英语。英语先用它形容风平浪静的海，随后扩展到人内心的平静，最后又变成动词，表示把人安抚下来。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses of calm grow from one picture: a flat surface with no wind on it.
sensesIntro.cn: calm 的三个义项都从同一个画面生长出来：一片没有风的平坦水面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a windless sea as flat as a mirror
core.cn: 核心意象：无风的海面像镜子一样平

branches.en: THE MIND: the quiet feeling is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 内心线：安静的情绪是最常用的义项。

branches.en: THE SOOTHING: the verb makes someone quiet.
branches.cn: 安抚线：动词使人安静下来。

branches.en: THE SEA: the windless surface is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 海面线：无风的水面是最古老的意思。

branches.en: THE STILLNESS: mind and sea share the same flat quiet.
branches.cn: 静止线：内心与海面共享同样的平坦安静。

branches.en: THE CHANGE: the verb moves a person into that quiet.
branches.cn: 转变线：动词把人带进那份安静。

definition_zh: 照相机；摄像机；（法律）非公开的、私下的
definition_en: a device that takes photographs or records video, or in law a hearing held in private

scene: 旅行时，他举起相机拍下了整片山谷。On the trip he raised his camera and photographed the whole valley.

derivatives.zh: 由 camera 与 man 组合而成，义为「摄影师」

senses.title: The device for photographs
senses.definition: a device with a lens that takes still photographs
senses.definitionCN: 带镜头、用于拍摄静止照片的设备
senses.example: On the trip he raised his camera and photographed the whole valley.
senses.exampleCN: 旅行时他举起相机拍下了整片山谷。
senses.why: Camera is short for camera obscura, a dark room that focused light to form an image.

senses.title: The device for video
senses.definition: a device that records moving pictures and sound
senses.definitionCN: 录制活动画面与声音的设备
senses.example: A camera followed the runner along the track.
senses.exampleCN: 一台摄像机沿着跑道跟拍那位跑者。
senses.why: Film and television kept the same Latin name for the machine that records moving images.
senses.whyCN: 电影与电视沿用了同一个拉丁名称，来指录制活动影像的机器。

senses.title: A private legal hearing
senses.definition: a court session held in private and closed to the public
senses.definitionCN: 不向公众开放、私下进行的法庭审理
senses.example: The judge heard the case in camera.
senses.exampleCN: 法官非公开审理了这起案件。
senses.why: In camera literally means in a chamber, and English law borrowed it for hearings held in a closed room.
senses.whyCN: in camera 字面意思是「在房间里」，英国法律借它指在关闭的房间内进行的审理。

intro.en: Camera is short for camera obscura, Latin for a dark room, because early cameras were darkened boxes that focused light.
intro.cn: camera 是 camera obscura 的缩写，拉丁语意为「暗室」，因为早期相机就是让光线聚焦的暗箱。

items.en: Camera meant a room or chamber in Latin.
items.cn: camera 在拉丁语中意为房间或室。

items.en: A camera obscura was a dark room with a small hole that threw an image on the wall.
items.cn: camera obscura 是一间开小孔的暗室，能把影像投在墙上。

items.en: Portable dark boxes replaced the room and kept the name camera.
items.cn: 便携的暗箱取代了房间，却保留了 camera 这个名字。

items.en: When light-sensitive plates appeared, the box became a camera that fixed the image.
items.cn: 当感光板出现，这个暗箱就成了能固定影像的照相机。

items.en: Today camera covers still, video and phone cameras, and the legal phrase in camera survives.
items.cn: 今天 camera 涵盖照相机、摄像机和手机镜头，法律短语 in camera 也仍在使用。

root: camera 是 camera obscura 的缩写，拉丁语意思是「暗室」。最早人们在一间关黑、只开小孔的房间外观察，光线穿过小孔会在墙上投出倒立的影像。后来这种房间被做成便携的暗箱，名字仍是 camera。感光板出现后，暗箱能够把影像固定下来，于是成了照相机；录制活动画面的机器沿用同一名称，成了摄像机。法律里 in camera 仍保留「在房间内」的旧义，指不公开的审理。

definition_zh: 营地；露营；阵营
definition_en: a place where people stay in tents, to live there for a short time, or a group that shares one belief
core_image: 草地上支起的一排帐篷
scene: 夏夜里，我们在湖边搭起帐篷宿营。That summer we camped by the lake.

derivatives.zh: 由 camp 加 -er 构成，义为「露营者；房车」

senses.title: The place with tents
senses.definition: a place where people stay in tents or small huts for a short time
senses.definitionCN: 人们短期住在帐篷或小屋里的地方
senses.example: The camp stood beside a quiet river.
senses.exampleCN: 营地坐落在一条安静的河边。
senses.why: The Latin campus meant a field, and armies spread their tents on just such an open field.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 campus 意为田野，军队正是在这样的空地上支起帐篷。

senses.title: To live in tents
senses.definition: to stay outdoors in a tent for a short time
senses.definitionCN: 在户外帐篷里短暂居住
senses.example: That summer we camped by the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 那年夏天我们在湖边宿营。
senses.why: The place name turned into the activity, so a camp became something people do.
senses.whyCN: 表示地点的名词变成了活动，于是 camp 成了人们做的事。

senses.title: A group with one belief
senses.definition: a group of people who share the same ideas in a dispute
senses.definitionCN: 争论中持相同看法的一群人
senses.example: The two camps could not agree on the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 两个阵营无法就这个方案达成一致。
senses.why: Armies camped apart on different sides, and the word for the ground became the word for the side.
senses.whyCN: 军队分开扎营、各占一边，表示地面的词就成了表示立场的词。

intro.en: Camp comes from Latin campus, a field, which also gave English the word campus for school grounds.
intro.cn: camp 来自拉丁语 campus，意为田野，英语里的 campus（校园）也出自同一个词。

items.en: Campus meant an open field or plain.
items.cn: campus 意为开阔的田野或平原。

items.en: Italian campo kept the field sense and added the sense of an army's ground.
items.cn: 意大利语 campo 保留田野义，又添了军队驻地的意思。

items.en: French camp named the place where an army pitched its tents.
items.cn: 法语 camp 指军队搭帐篷驻扎的地方。

items.en: English borrowed camp for both the tents and the act of staying there.
items.cn: 英语借入 camp，同时指帐篷营地与在那里居住的行为。

items.en: The word widened to holiday camps, summer camps and rival camps in an argument.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到度假营、夏令营，以及争论中的对立阵营。

senses.title: To be able to

senses.example: She can swim the whole length of the pool.

senses.why: Old English cunnan meant to know how, and knowing how is still the heart of can.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 cunnan 意为知道怎么做，而「知道怎么做」至今仍是 can 的核心。

senses.title: To be allowed to
senses.definition: to be allowed to do something
senses.definitionCN: 被允许做某事
senses.example: You can borrow my bike this afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 今天下午你可以借我的自行车。
senses.why: If you know how to act and nothing stops you, people say you can do it.
senses.whyCN: 当你懂得怎么做、又没有阻碍时，人们就说你可以做这件事。

senses.title: A metal container
senses.definition: a metal container used to keep food or drink
senses.definitionCN: 用来盛放食物或饮料的金属容器
senses.example: He opened a can of soup for lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 他午饭时开了一罐汤。
senses.why: This sense is a separate Old English word, canne, meaning a container, which simply shares the spelling.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自另一个古英语词 canne，意为容器，只是与情态动词同形。

intro.en: Can has two origins that look alike: a verb meaning to know how, and a noun meaning a container.
intro.cn: can 有两个看起来相同的来源：一个表示「知道怎么做」的动词，和一个表示容器的名词。

items.en: Cunnan meant to know or know how, the source of the verb can.
items.cn: cunnan 意为知道或懂得，是动词 can 的来源。

items.en: Canne meant a container, the source of the noun can.
items.cn: canne 意为容器，是名词 can 的来源。

items.en: The past tense could came from cuþe, and it later took on a polite sense.
items.cn: 过去式 could 来自 cuþe，后来发展出客气的用法。

items.en: Metal cans for preserved food spread the container sense in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪保存食物的金属罐让容器义广为流传。

items.en: Today can covers ability, permission and the everyday food can.
items.cn: 今天 can 同时表示能力、许可和日常的食品罐头。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second collects other containers and modals.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收其他容器与情态词。

normal.cn: 它常与 soup、opener、tin、help 搭配。

abstract.en: See a tight fist that says I know how: that fist is can.
abstract.cn: 想象一只握紧的拳头，表示「我会」：那只拳头就是 can。

abstract.en: Open the fist and a metal can appears in the same hand.
abstract.cn: 张开拳头，同一只手里出现一只金属罐。

abstract.en: Let the fist open into a can whenever you need the word.
abstract.cn: 需要这个词时，就让拳头张开成一只罐头。

root: can 其实是两个同形的词。作情态动词时，它来自古英语 cunnan，意思是「知道、懂得怎么做」，所以 can 至今表示能力；它的过去式 could 来自 cuþe，后来还发展出委婉请求的用法。作名词时，它来自另一个古英语词 canne，意思是容器，十九世纪金属罐头普及后，这个义项大为流行。两条来源拼写相同，今天 can 同时覆盖能力、许可和罐头三层意思。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses of can come from two old words that now share one spelling: knowing how, and a container.
sensesIntro.cn: can 的三个义项来自两个如今同形的古词：懂得怎么做，以及一个容器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a firm grip on a solid metal can

branches.en: THE ABILITY: knowing how is the first sense.
branches.cn: 能力线：懂得怎么做是第一个义项。

branches.en: THE PERMISSION: being free to act is the second sense.
branches.cn: 许可线：不受阻拦地去做是第二个义项。

branches.en: THE CONTAINER: the metal can is a separate old word.
branches.cn: 容器线：金属罐来自另一个古词。

branches.en: THE MODAL: ability and permission share one grammar.
branches.cn: 情态线：能力与许可共用同一套语法。

branches.cn: 保存线：密封的罐头让食物能存放多年。

definition_zh: 取消；撤销；抵消
definition_en: to stop a planned event, to withdraw an order or decision, or to balance out an effect
core_image: 一支笔在日程表的一行上划掉一道斜线
scene: 下雨了，他们只好取消下午的球赛。Because of the rain they had to cancel the afternoon match.
sceneCN: 这里 cancel 是「取消」（第 1 个义项：停止已安排好的活动）；句意为因为下雨他们只好取消下午的球赛。

derivatives.zh: 由 cancel 加 -ation 构成，义为「取消；撤销」
由 cancel 加 -er 构成，义为「取消者」
由 cancel 加 -able 构成，义为「可取消的」

senses.title: To stop a planned event
senses.definition: to say that a planned event will not happen
senses.definitionCN: 宣布已安排的活动不再举行
senses.example: Because of the rain they had to cancel the afternoon match.
senses.exampleCN: 因为下雨他们只好取消下午的球赛。
senses.why: The Latin cancelli were the crossed bars of a fence, and to cancel was to cross out with lattice marks.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 cancelli 是交叉的栅栏条，cancel 最初就是用交叉的格子线划掉字迹。

senses.title: To withdraw an order
senses.definition: to withdraw an order, a decision or an agreement
senses.definitionCN: 撤回订单、决定或协议
senses.example: She cancelled the order before it was sent.
senses.exampleCN: 她在发货前撤销了订单。
senses.why: Crossing out a written line ended it, so cancel came to mean ending an official order.
senses.whyCN: 在书面文字上划掉一条就等于终止它，于是 cancel 有了终止正式命令的意思。

senses.title: To balance out an effect
senses.definition: to stop one effect by an equal opposite one
senses.definitionCN: 用相等而相反的作用抵消某种效果
senses.example: The two teams cancelled out each other's strengths.
senses.exampleCN: 两支队伍互相抵消了对方的优势。
senses.why: Two crossed strokes wipe each other out, and that picture became the sense of balancing effects.
senses.whyCN: 两笔交叉的划线互相抹掉，这个画面就成了抵消效果的意思。

intro.en: Cancel comes from Latin cancelli, the crossed bars of a lattice, because crossing out a line looked like a small fence.
intro.cn: cancel 来自拉丁语 cancelli，指交叉的栅栏条，因为在文字上划掉一笔就像画了一道小栅栏。

items.en: Cancelli were the crossed bars that made a lattice or fence.
items.cn: cancelli 是构成格子或栅栏的交叉木条。

items.en: Cancellare meant to draw a lattice over writing, and so to cross it out.
items.cn: cancellare 意为在文字上画格子线，也就是划掉。

items.en: Old French cancellers carried the crossing-out sense into law and writing.
items.cn: 古法语 cancellers 把划掉的意思带进法律与文书。

items.en: English cancel first meant to cross out a document and void it.
items.cn: 英语 cancel 最初指在文件上划线使其作废。

items.en: The word widened to events, orders and opposing effects.
items.cn: 这个词后来扩展到活动、订单和相互抵消的作用。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second collects ways of ending a plan.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收终止计划的词。

normal.cn: 拉丁语 cancelli 是交叉的木条，而在文字上划掉一笔至今仍是取消。

normal.en: Cancel first meant to void a document by drawing lines through it.

normal.en: An order, a flight and a match can all be cancelled.
normal.cn: 订单、航班和比赛都可以被取消。

normal.en: It often pairs with flight, order, meeting and out.

abstract.cn: 想象一支笔在某个日期上划下一道斜线：那道线就是 cancel。

abstract.en: Draw a second line across the first and the two strokes wipe each other out.
abstract.cn: 在第一道上再划一道，两笔就互相抹掉了。

abstract.en: Keep the crossed date in mind and it will give you the word.
abstract.cn: 记住那个被划掉的日期，它就会把这个词交给你。

root: cancel 来自拉丁语 cancelli，指交叉排列的栅栏条。由它派生的 cancellare 意为在文字上画格子线，也就是划掉作废。这个词经古法语 canceller 进入英语，最初专指在文件上划线使其失效，后来扩展到取消活动、撤销订单。两笔交叉的划线互相抹掉，又生出「抵消」的意思，如两种力量 cancel out。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses of cancel grow from one picture: a line drawn through writing to void it.
sensesIntro.cn: cancel 的三个义项都从同一个画面生长出来：在文字上划一道线使其作废。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pen drawing one slanted line through a date
core.cn: 核心意象：一支笔在日程表的一行上划掉一道斜线

branches.en: THE EVENT: crossing out a date stops the plan.
branches.cn: 活动线：把日期划掉就停止了计划。

branches.en: THE ORDER: the same stroke voids a written order.
branches.cn: 命令线：同一道划线让书面命令作废。

branches.en: THE BALANCE: two opposite strokes wipe each other out.
branches.cn: 平衡线：两道相反的划线互相抹掉。

branches.en: THE WRITING: events and orders both die on paper.
branches.cn: 书面线：活动与命令都在纸面上被终止。

branches.en: THE REVERSAL: withdrawing and balancing both undo a force.
branches.cn: 反转线：撤回与抵消都在撤掉一股力量。
